messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGER — p99 latency breach detected on router-prod-us-east. p99 across streaming routes > 6.2s (SLO 1.5s). Alert rules triggered: router.p99 > 5s for 5m. Paging sara (primary oncall).
sara: reading into it now. attaching dashboard link: https://console.redwood/infer/dashboard/router-prod-us-east/p99
jen: I'm seeing spikes aligned with a single backend pool (lb-pool-eus1-42). Tail stalls + increased queue times on that pool.
mike: router logs show a large number of sticky routes pinned to backend node ip 10.3.42.7 — seems like a routing hash skew. Querying routing policy revisions.
sara: any deploys in last hour? deploy-bot: 1837542000 - routing-policy: roll #112 applied to prod east at 1837542120 by infra-release-bot
mike: that rollout changed weighted routing logic to favor node locality for streaming to reduce cold-starts. suspect: a bug in weight normalization produced fractional weights -> one hot partition.
leo: Customer impact: CS reports 3 customers with degraded streaming (long stalls) — priority-2. cs-ops: ticket #CS-8792 opened.
sara: mitigation plan: 1) remove new routing weights (rollback policy) 2) drain hot backend 10.3.42.7 3) enable fallback to alternate pool for streaming. Doing step 1.
mike: rolling rollback to prev routing-policy (112 -> 111). Command:

```
infractl routing apply --env prod --region us-east --policy routing-policy@111
```

Executing now.
sara: rollback applied at 1837543281. Observability: p95 down to 900ms, p99 still ~3.8s but trending down.
jen: starting drain of 10.3.42.7 from lb-pool-eus1-42. Command:

```
kubectl annotate node 10.3.42.7 redwood/drain=scheduled
kubectl cordon node 10.3.42.7
kubectl drain node 10.3.42.7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

Drain started 1837543340.
mike: also adding a temporary routing override to cap per-key affinity to avoid hot keys. Patch:

```
policy.patch: set affinity.max_per_key=8
apply: infractl routing patch --env prod --region us-east --policy-temp cap-affinity-8
```

Applying cap-affinity-8 at 1837543382.
leo: telemetry: p99 dropped to 1.8s after cap-affinity and drain in progress. Some streaming stalls remain but endpoints are recovering. CS updated customers.
cs-ops: Customer A (enterprise) reported session resets between 1837543000-1837543300, now mostly resolved. They've opened for post-incident debrief.
sara: good. need to hand off to night oncall in 15m. mike / jen, can you take a look at root cause? I want a short postmortem skeleton: timeline, code change (weight normalization), mitigation steps, follow-ups (add e2e for weight normalization, add alarm for pool skew). I'll page next oncall.
mike: taking lead on RCA. preliminary: rounding bug in normalization routine when sum(weights) < 1e-9 on float64 underflow for certain locality configs. Repro on staging: yes.
jen: operations follow-ups: 1) add pool skew metric alert (backend_share_entropy < threshold) 2) add automatic temporary fallback after 30s of sustained hot-partition 3) document manual drain runbook for lb-pool.
sara: handing off. next oncall is leo, timestamp handoff: 1837543450. leo, you're on deck; contact list: mike, jen, sara.
leo: acknowledged. I'll monitor for 1 hour and coordinate RCA write-up with mike. Also will confirm drained node rejoin and load rebalancing.
deploy-bot: rollout status: routing-policy@111 confirmed active at 1837543290.
sara: post-incident notes: severity P2 (partial SLO breach, customer-facing stalls). Actions taken: rollback routing-policy, drained hot node, cap affinity, opened CS tickets. Next: RCA draft by mike due EOD, follow-up runbook by jen, add synthetic tests for routing weight normalization (engineers + QE).
mike: will include a minimal reproducer and patch PR to fix normalization in the routing weight calculator. PR target: 1837549999.
cs-ops: Will schedule customer debriefs for impacted accounts tomorrow 10:00 ET.
sara: closing the immediate paging stream. If any regression within next 60m, re-pagering rules active. :thumbsup:
